cards.power: TAKE half of target player's resource tokens. You own their merch, touring, and soul.
cards.lore: They say it's a partnership. A tick also calls the dog a partner.
cards.gradeReason: Classic predatory contract villain. Immediately embodied, zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink cartoon. Subject: Octopus in suit signing contract with small rabbit. Mood: Predatory menace.

cards.power: GAIN +2 Hype, but cannot read card text for the next 3 turns.
cards.lore: I coulda been a contender! Instead, I'm a tax write-off.
cards.gradeReason: Wide-eyed innocent archetype, penalty is performative. No context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor cartoon. Subject: Starry-eyed lamb with guitar before towering record label. Mood: Innocent vulnerability.

cards.power: FORCE a player to re-roll. If they fail, you keep their dice.
cards.lore: Don't worry about the fine print, kid. It's just standard boilerplate for 'indentured servitude'.
cards.gradeReason: Classic music-biz predator. The quote is immediately quotable at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink cartoon. Subject: Suited hyena waving contract at small terrified musician. Mood: Slick predatory threat.

cards.power: NEGATE any 'Success' roll. The label recoups expenses first.
cards.lore: Hollywood Accounting: Where a billion dollars in profit is technically a loss.
cards.gradeReason: Sharp concept, but Hollywood Accounting reference requires industry context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Noir cartoon. Subject: Magnifying glass over contract, dollar signs vanishing into tiny text. Mood: Claustrophobic dread.

cards.power: SPEND 5 Coin to force your song to the top of the playlist.
cards.lore: Screw the rules, I have money! It's not bribery if we call it 'promotional support'.
cards.gradeReason: 'Screw the rules, I have money!' is immediately quotable and performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corrupted pop art cartoon. Subject: Pig bribing radio tower operator with stacks of cash. Mood: Gleefully corrupt.

cards.power: START the game on Level 3. Talent is optional; lineage is mandatory.
cards.lore: An industry plant with roots in the boardroom. Born on third base, thinks they hit a triple.
cards.gradeReason: Universal archetype. 'Born on third base, thinks they hit a triple' is a G1 lore line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gilded cartoon. Subject: Peacock hatching from golden egg on boardroom throne. Mood: Entitled arrogance.

cards.power: COPY the last played effect. Follow the leader into the abyss.
cards.lore: Manufactured buzz for a disposable generation. Trending today, deleted tomorrow.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanic clear, but 'follow the leader into the abyss' is abstract rather than performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Digital glitch cartoon. Subject: Hamsters blindly following each other off a cliff. Mood: Cheerful oblivion.

cards.power: STEAL the credit for another player's success roll.

cards.gradeReason: 'You provide the face, we provide the feelings' is devastating and instantly performed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Shadow cartoon. Subject: Parrot performing onstage while fox writes lyrics in background. Mood: Hollow celebrity.

cards.power: CHANGE the genre of any card in play to 'Pop'.
cards.lore: I don't hear a single. Can you make it sound more like that other song everyone likes?
cards.gradeReason: Classic industry villain. The lore quote is instantly quotable and immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate cartoon. Subject: Vulture in suit overriding all mixing board knobs. Mood: Control-freak energy.

cards.power: DISCARD your hand and draw new cards until the demographic approves.
cards.lore: We pivoted to appeal to males 18-34, so your ballad is now a truck commercial.
cards.gradeReason: Great mechanic, but demographic marketing context needed for full punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Boardroom cartoon. Subject: Panel of sheep with YES/NO signs judging terrified musician. Mood: Conformist pressure.

cards.power: PREDICT the next card. If it matches the formula, double its effect.
cards.lore: The Scorpion Algorithm: Optimizing art until it is perfectly flat and universally tolerated.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but abstract mechanism. 'Scorpion Algorithm' name needs unpacking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Digital horror cartoon. Subject: Giant spider in server rack predicting music charts. Mood: Cold optimization.

cards.power: IGNORE penalties if you switch styles this turn.
cards.lore: Forced Pivot. Yesterday you were Country, today you're EDM. Try to keep up.
cards.gradeReason: 'Forced Pivot' requires context; the lore explains rather than invites.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Chameleon cartoon. Subject: Lizard switching between cowboy hat and DJ helmet mid-performance. Mood: Frantic reinvention.

cards.power: DESTROY a card to 'improve' it. It comes back with lower stats.
cards.lore: My vision is the only vision. You're just the meat holding the instrument.
cards.gradeReason: 'You're just the meat holding the instrument' — devastating, instantly performed. Strong G1.

cards.power: FIX a failed roll. The result is successful but artificial.

cards.gradeReason: 'Talent is a bug. Pitch correction is the feature.' — perfect inverted-tech lore. G1.

cards.power: SWAP this card in to take the damage for another player.
cards.lore: The nameless pro who actually played on your favorite album. No royalties, flat fee.
cards.gradeReason: Sympathetic character, clear mechanic, but role is passive. Works at table, not a knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Melancholy cartoon. Subject: Horse playing drums alone in dark studio, no name on credits. Mood: Professional resignation.

cards.power: SKIP your turn. Repeat indefinitely until contract expires.
cards.lore: The label isn't saying "no." They're just saying "not in this lifetime."
cards.gradeReason: SKIP mechanic is passive. Lore is strong but card invites no active behavior.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kafkaesque cartoon. Subject: Demo tape imprisoned in filing cabinet labeled 'Not In This Lifetime'. Mood: Institutional limbo.

cards.power: SACRIFICE the rest of your hand to play this one card.

cards.gradeReason: Dramatic sacrifice mechanic mirrors real-career stakes. Lore is perfectly biting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Golden egg cartoon. Subject: Gleaming golden single on pedestal surrounded by discarded filler tracks. Mood: Pyrrhic victory.

cards.power: BLOCK an opponent's action unless they pay you a royalty.

cards.power: OVERPOWER all other cards this turn. No dynamic range allowed.

cards.gradeReason: 'Brickwalled audio' needs music production context. G1 with a music-literate crowd.

cards.power: ROLL a D6. On 1-3, your career ends immediately.

cards.gradeReason: D6 career-death mechanic is dramatic. Lore is perfect but power is a passive roll.

cards.power: GAIN Appeal, LOSE Dignity.

cards.power: DISGUISE your true type. Opponents cannot target you this turn.

cards.power: GENERATE hype by attacking an ally. No actual damage dealt.

cards.power: EXHAUST this card to gain quick cash. Discard after 3 turns.

cards.power: EXPAND your reach. Collect tokens from players outside your genre.

cards.power: GAIN massive resources, but your 'Credibility' score drops to zero.

cards.gradeReason: 'From protest songs to insurance jingles' — perfectly captures the sell-out moment. G1.

cards.power: BIND a fan to your card. They cannot leave play but drain your energy.

cards.power: FORCE a player to perform an action they don't want to do.

verdict: Sonic Slaughterhouse walks into the room and immediately eats the music industry's lunch — then charges them for the napkin. The five-phase architecture (Bait → Studio → Image → Grinder → Landfill → Resistance) is the tightest structural narrative in this corpus; every phase title doubles as a performance cue. 'The Unreleased Masterpiece' — a card that CANNOT be played and exists only as a rumor — is the kind of meta-genius that makes me want to quit and start over. Named weakness: The Tour Bus card has a layout hiccup that mangles its power/lore split, and The Lip Sync is missing its lore text entirely. Table-ready? Yes — with surgical fixes before Gumroad launch.
blurb: The complete playbook of music industry exploitation, from the 360 deal to the posthumous hologram tour. For anyone who's sold out a venue and never got paid. Play it loud. Don't feed the executives.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: SONIC SLAUGHTERHOUSE – The Music Industry, Cut and Played for Parts (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

The music industry is a slaughterhouse with a merch table out front.

A kid signs the 360 deal because the pen is warm and everyone in the room is smiling. Then the line starts moving. The studio sands the weird edges off the songs until they test clean with a focus group the band has never met. Marketing fits the costume, picks the demographic, and ships the rebrand before the first record is even cold.
